NASB.1: The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea. As windstorms in the Negev sweep on, It comes from the wilderness, from a terrifying land.
NASB.2: A harsh vision has been shown to me; The treacherous one [still] deals treacherously, and the destroyer [still] destroys. Go up, Elam, lay siege, Media; I have made an end of all the groaning she has caused.
NASB.3: For this reason my loins are full of anguish; Pains have seized me like the pains of a woman in labor. I am so bewildered I cannot hear, so terrified I cannot see.
NASB.4: My mind reels, horror overwhelms me; The twilight I longed for has been turned for me into trembling.
NASB.5: They set the table, they spread out the cloth, they eat, they drink; 'Rise up, captains, oil the shields,'
NASB.6: For thus the Lord says to me, 'Go, station the lookout, let him report what he sees.
NASB.7: 'When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs, A train of donkeys, a train of camels, Let him pay close attention, very close attention.'
NASB.8: Then the lookout called, 'O Lord, I stand continually by day on the watchtower, And I am stationed every night at my guard post.
NASB.9: 'Now behold, here comes a troop of riders, horsemen in pairs.' And one said, 'Fallen, fallen is Babylon; And all the images of her gods are shattered on the ground.'
NASB.10: O my threshed [people], and my afflicted of the threshing floor! What I have heard from the LORD of hosts, The God of Israel, I make known to you.
NASB.11: The oracle concerning Edom. One keeps calling to me from Seir, 'Watchman, how far gone is the night? Watchman, how far gone is the night?'
NASB.12: The watchman says, 'Morning comes but also night. If you would inquire, inquire; Come back again.'
NASB.13: The oracle about Arabia. In the thickets of Arabia you must spend the night, O caravans of Dedanites.
NASB.14: Bring water for the thirsty, O inhabitants of the land of Tema, Meet the fugitive with bread.
NASB.15: For they have fled from the swords, From the drawn sword, and from the bent bow And from the press of battle.
NASB.16: For thus the Lord said to me, 'In a year, as a hired man would count it, all the splendor of Kedar will terminate;
NASB.17: and the remainder of the number of bowmen, the mighty men of the sons of Kedar, will be few; for the LORD God of Israel has spoken.'

ESV.1: The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea. As whirlwinds in the Negeb sweep on, it comes from the wilderness, from a terrible land.
ESV.2: A stern vision is told to me; the traitor betrays, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, O Elam; lay siege, O Media; all the sighing she has caused I bring to an end.
ESV.3: Therefore my loins are filled with anguish; pangs have seized me, like the pangs of a woman in labor; I am bowed down so that I cannot hear; I am dismayed so that I cannot see.
ESV.4: My heart staggers; horror has appalled me; the twilight I longed for has been turned for me into trembling.
ESV.5: They prepare the table, they spread the rugs,  they eat, they drink. Arise, O princes; oil the shield!
ESV.6: For thus the Lord said to me: “Go, set a watchman; let him announce what he sees.
ESV.7: When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, let him listen diligently, very diligently.”
ESV.8: Then he who saw cried out:  “Upon a watchtower I stand, O Lord, continually by day, and at my post I am stationed whole nights.
ESV.9: And behold, here come riders, horsemen in pairs!” And he answered, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the carved images of her gods he has shattered to the ground.”
ESV.10: O my threshed and winnowed one, what I have heard from the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, I announce to you.
ESV.11: The oracle concerning Dumah. One is calling to me from Seir, “Watchman, what time of the night? Watchman, what time of the night?”
ESV.12: The watchman says: “Morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire; come back again.”
ESV.13: The oracle concerning Arabia. In the thickets in Arabia you will lodge, O caravans of Dedanites.
ESV.14: To the thirsty bring water; meet the fugitive with bread, O inhabitants of the land of Tema.
ESV.15: For they have fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the press of battle.
ESV.16: For thus the Lord said to me, “Within a year, according to the years of a hired worker, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end.
ESV.17: And the remainder of the archers of the mighty men of the sons of Kedar will be few, for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.”

NKJV.1: The burden against the Wilderness of the Sea. As whirlwinds in the South pass through, So it comes from the desert, from a terrible land.
NKJV.2: A distressing vision is declared to me;  The treacherous dealer deals treacherously, And the plunderer plunders.  Go up, O Elam! Besiege, O Media! All its sighing I have made to cease.
NKJV.3: Therefore my loins are filled with pain; Pangs have taken hold of me, like the pangs of a woman in labor. I was distressed when I heard it; I was dismayed when I saw it.
NKJV.4: My heart wavered, fearfulness frightened me;  The night for which I longed He turned into fear for me.
NKJV.5: Prepare the table, Set a watchman in the tower, Eat and drink. Arise, you princes, Anoint the shield!
NKJV.6: For thus has the Lord said to me: “Go, set a watchman, Let him declare what he sees.”
NKJV.7: And he saw a chariot with a pair of horsemen, A chariot of donkeys, and a chariot of camels, And he listened earnestly with great care.
NKJV.8: Then he cried, “A lion, my Lord! I stand continually on the watchtower in the daytime; I have sat at my post every night.
NKJV.9: And look, here comes a chariot of men with a pair of horsemen!” Then he answered and said, “Babylon is fallen, is fallen! And all the carved images of her gods He has broken to the ground.”
NKJV.10: Oh, my threshing and the grain of my floor! That which I have heard from the LORD of hosts, The God of Israel, I have declared to you.
NKJV.11: The burden against Dumah. He calls to me out of Seir, “Watchman, what of the night? Watchman, what of the night?”
NKJV.12: The watchman said, “The morning comes, and also the night. If you will inquire, inquire; Return! Come back!”
NKJV.13: The burden against Arabia. In the forest in Arabia you will lodge, O you traveling companies of Dedanites.
NKJV.14: O inhabitants of the land of Tema, Bring water to him who is thirsty; With their bread they met him who fled.
NKJV.15: For they fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, From the bent bow, and from the distress of war.
NKJV.16: For thus the LORD has said to me: “Within a year, according to the year of a hired man, all the glory of Kedar will fail;
NKJV.17: and the remainder of the number of archers, the mighty men of the people of Kedar, will be diminished; for the LORD God of Israel has spoken it.”

WEB.1: The burden of the wilderness of the sea. As whirlwinds in the South sweep through, it comes from the wilderness, from an awesome land.
WEB.2: A grievous vision is declared to me. The treacherous man deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam; attack! I have stopped all of Media’s sighing.

WEB.4: My heart flutters. Horror has frightened me. The twilight that I desired has been turned into trembling for me.
WEB.5: They prepare the table. They set the watch. They eat. They drink. Rise up, you princes, oil the shield!
WEB.6: For the Lord said to me, “Go, set a watchman. Let him declare what he sees.
WEB.7: When he sees a troop, horsemen in pairs, a troop of donkeys, a troop of camels, he shall listen diligently with great attentiveness.”

WEB.9: Behold, here comes a troop of men, horsemen in pairs.” He answered, “Fallen, fallen is Babylon; and all the engraved images of her gods are broken to the ground.
WEB.10: You are my threshing, and the grain of my floor!” That which I have heard from Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, I have declared to you.

WEB.15: For they fled away from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.
WEB.16: For the Lord said to me, “Within a year, as a worker bound by contract would count it, all the glory of Kedar will fail,
WEB.17: and the residue of the number of the archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar, will be few; for Yahweh, the God of Israel, has spoken it.”

NLT.1:
This message came to me concerning Babylon — the desert by the sea : Disaster is roaring down on you from the desert,
like a whirlwind sweeping in from the Negev.
NLT.2:
I see a terrifying vision:
I see the betrayer betraying,
the destroyer destroying.
Go ahead, you Elamites and Medes,
attack and lay siege.
I will make an end
to all the groaning Babylon caused.
NLT.3:
My stomach aches and burns with pain.
Sharp pangs of anguish are upon me,
like those of a woman in labor.
I grow faint when I hear what God is planning;
I am too afraid to look.
NLT.4:
My mind reels and my heart races.
I longed for evening to come,
but now I am terrified of the dark.
NLT.5:
Look! They are preparing a great feast.
They are spreading rugs for people to sit on.
Everyone is eating and drinking.
But quick! Grab your shields and prepare for battle.
You are being attacked!
NLT.6:
Meanwhile, the Lord said to me,
“Put a watchman on the city wall.
Let him shout out what he sees.
NLT.7:
He should look for chariots
drawn by pairs of horses,
and for riders on donkeys and camels.
Let the watchman be fully alert.”
NLT.8:
Then the watchman called out,
“Day after day I have stood on the watchtower, my lord.
Night after night I have remained at my post.
NLT.9:
Now at last — look!
Here comes a man in a chariot
with a pair of horses!”
Then the watchman said,
“Babylon is fallen, fallen!
All the idols of Babylon
lie broken on the ground!”
NLT.10:
O my people, threshed and winnowed,
I have told you everything the LORD of Heaven’s Armies has said,
everything the God of Israel has told me.
NLT.11:
This message came to me concerning Edom : Someone from Edom keeps calling to me,
“Watchman, how much longer until morning?
When will the night be over?”
NLT.12:
The watchman replies,
“Morning is coming, but night will soon return.
If you wish to ask again, then come back and ask.”
NLT.13:
This message came to me concerning Arabia: O caravans from Dedan,
hide in the deserts of Arabia.
NLT.14:
O people of Tema,
bring water to these thirsty people,
food to these weary refugees.
NLT.15:
They have fled from the sword,
from the drawn sword,
from the bent bow
and the terrors of battle.
NLT.16: The Lord said to me, “Within a year, counting each day, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end.
NLT.17: Only a few of its courageous archers will survive. I, the LORD, the God of Israel, have spoken!”

AMP.1:
The [mournful, inspired] oracle ( a burden to be carried) concerning the Desert of the Sea (the seasonally flooded plains just south of Babylon):
As windstorms in the Negev (the South) sweep through,
So it (God's judgment) comes from the desert, from [the hostile armies of] a terrifying land.
AMP.2:
A harsh vision has been shown to me;
The treacherous one deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys.
Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media!
All the groaning [caused by Babylon's ruthless oppressions] I [the LORD] have brought to an end.
AMP.3:
Therefore [continues Isaiah] my loins are filled with anguish;
Pains have seized me like the pains of a woman in childbirth;
I am so bent and bewildered that I cannot hear, I am so terrified that I cannot see.
AMP.4:
My mind reels, horror overwhelms me;
The twilight I longed for has been turned into fear and trembling for me.
AMP.5:
They set the table [for the doomed banquet], they spread out the cloth, they eat, they drink;
"Rise up, captains [of Belshazzar's court], oil your shields [for battle, for your enemy is at the gates]!"
AMP.6:
This is what the Lord says to me,
"Go, station the lookout, let him report what he sees.
AMP.7:
"When he sees a chariot, horsemen in pairs,
A train of donkeys and a train of camels,
Let him pay attention and listen closely, very closely."
AMP.8:
And the lookout called like a lion,
"O Lord, I stand continually on the watchtower by day,
And I am stationed every night at my guard post.
AMP.9:
"Now look! Here comes a troop of riders, horsemen in pairs."
And one said, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon;
And all the carved images of her gods are shattered on the ground."
AMP.10:
O my threshed people [Judah, who must be judged and trampled down by Babylon], my afflicted of the threshing floor.
What I have heard from the LORD of hosts,
The God of Israel, I have [joyfully] announced to you [that Babylon is to fall].
AMP.11:
The [mournful, inspired] oracle ( a burden to be carried) concerning Dumah (Edom):
Someone keeps calling to me from Seir (Edom),
"Watchman, what is left of the night [of Assyrian oppression]?
Watchman, what is left of the night? [How long until morning?]"
AMP.12:
The watchman says,
"The morning comes [only briefly], but also [comes] the night [of Babylonian oppression].
If you would ask [of me then], ask [again, if Edom really wishes to know];
Come back again."
AMP.13:
The [mournful, inspired] oracle ( a burden to be carried) concerning Arabia:
In the thickets of Arabia you must spend the night,
Caravans of Dedanites.
AMP.14:
Bring water for the thirsty [Dedanites],
O inhabitants of the land of Tema [in Arabia];
Meet the fugitive with bread.
AMP.15:
For they have fled from the swords,
From the drawn sword, from the bent bow
And from the press of battle and grief of war.
AMP.16: For the Lord has said this to me, "Within a year, according to the years of a hired man [who will work no longer than was agreed], all the splendor of [the tribe of] Kedar will end;
AMP.17: and the remainder of the number of archers, the mighty men of the sons of Kedar, will be few; for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken."

NIV.1:
A Prophecy Against Babylon
An oracle concerning the Desert by the Sea:
Like whirlwinds sweeping through the southland,
an invader comes from the desert,
from a land of terror.
NIV.2:
A dire vision has been shown to me:
The traitor betrays, the looter takes loot.
Elam, attack! Media, lay siege!
I will bring to an end all the groaning she caused.
NIV.3:
At this my body is racked with pain,
pangs seize me, like those of a woman in labor;
I am staggered by what I hear,
I am bewildered by what I see.
NIV.4:
My heart falters,
fear makes me tremble;
the twilight I longed for
has become a horror to me.
NIV.5:
They set the tables,
they spread the rugs,
they eat, they drink!
Get up, you officers,
oil the shields!
NIV.6:
This is what the Lord says to me:
“Go, post a lookout
and have him report what he sees.
NIV.7:
When he sees chariots
with teams of horses,
riders on donkeys
or riders on camels,
let him be alert,
fully alert.”
NIV.8:
And the lookout shouted,
“Day after day, my lord, I stand on the watchtower;
every night I stay at my post.
NIV.9:
Look, here comes a man in a chariot
with a team of horses.
And he gives back the answer:
‘Babylon has fallen, has fallen!
All the images of its gods
lie shattered on the ground!’”
NIV.10:
O my people, crushed on the threshing floor,
I tell you what I have heard
from the Lord Almighty,
from the God of Israel.
NIV.11:
A Prophecy Against Edom
An oracle concerning Dumah:
Someone calls to me from Seir,
“Watchman, what is left of the night?
Watchman, what is left of the night?”
NIV.12:
The watchman replies,
“Morning is coming, but also the night.
If you would ask, then ask;
and come back yet again.”
NIV.13:
A Prophecy Against Arabia
An oracle concerning Arabia:
You caravans of Dedanites,
who camp in the thickets of Arabia,
NIV.14:
bring water for the thirsty;
you who live in Tema,
bring food for the fugitives.
NIV.15:
They flee from the sword,
from the drawn sword,
from the bent bow
and from the heat of battle.
NIV.16: This is what the Lord says to me: “Within one year, as a servant bound by contract would count it, all the pomp of Kedar will come to an end.
NIV.17: The survivors of the bowmen, the warriors of Kedar, will be few.” The Lord, the God of Israel, has spoken.

A Message concerning the desert at the sea:
As tempests drive through the Negev Desert,
coming out of the desert, that terror-filled place,
MSG.2:
A hard vision is given me:
The betrayer betrayed, the plunderer plundered.
Attack, Elam!
Lay siege, Media!
Persians, attack!
Attack, Babylon!
I'll put an end to
all the moaning and groaning.
MSG.3:
Because of this news I'm doubled up in pain,
writhing in pain like a woman having a baby,
Baffled by what I hear,
undone by what I see.
MSG.4:
Absolutely stunned,
horror-stricken,
I had hoped for a relaxed evening,
but it has turned into a nightmare.
MSG.5:
The banquet is spread,
the guests reclining in luxurious ease,
Eating and drinking, having a good time,
and then, "To arms, princes! The fight is on!"
MSG.6:
The Master told me, "Go, post a lookout.
Have him report whatever he spots.
MSG.7:
When he sees horses and wagons in battle formation,
lines of donkeys and columns of camels,
Tell him to keep his ear to the ground,
note every whisper, every rumor."
MSG.8:
Just then, the lookout shouted,
"I'm at my post, Master,
Sticking to my post day after day
and all through the night!
MSG.9:
I watched them come,
the horses and wagons in battle formation.
I heard them call out the war news in headlines:
'Babylon fallen! Fallen!
And all its precious god-idols
smashed to pieces on the ground.' "
MSG.10:
Dear Israel, you've been through a lot,
you've been put through the mill.
The good news I get from God-of-the-Angel-Armies,
the God of Israel, I now pass on to you.
MSG.11:
A Message concerning Edom:
A voice calls to me
from the Seir mountains in Edom,
"Night watchman! How long till daybreak?
How long will this night last?"
MSG.12:
The night watchman calls back,
"Morning's coming,
But for now it's still night.
If you ask me again, I'll give the same answer."
MSG.13:
A Message concerning Arabia:
You'll have to camp out in the desert badlands,
you caravans of Dedanites.
MSG.14:
Haul water to the thirsty,
greet fugitives with bread.
Show your desert hospitality,
you who live in Tema.
MSG.15:
The desert's swarming with refugees
escaping the horrors of war.
MSG.16: The Master told me, "Hang on. Within one year—I'll sign a contract on it!—the arrogant brutality of Kedar, those hooligans of the desert, will be over,
MSG.17: nothing much left of the Kedar toughs." The God of Israel says so.

NRSVCE.1:
The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea. As whirlwinds in the Negeb sweep on,
it comes from the desert,
from a terrible land.
NRSVCE.2:
A stern vision is told to me;
the betrayer betrays,
and the destroyer destroys.
Go up, O Elam,
lay siege, O Media;
all the sighing she has caused
I bring to an end.
NRSVCE.3:
Therefore my loins are filled with anguish;
pangs have seized me,
like the pangs of a woman in labor;
I am bowed down so that I cannot hear,
I am dismayed so that I cannot see.
NRSVCE.4:
My mind reels, horror has appalled me;
the twilight I longed for
has been turned for me into trembling.
NRSVCE.5:
They prepare the table,
they spread the rugs,
they eat, they drink.
Rise up, commanders,
oil the shield!
NRSVCE.6:
For thus the Lord said to me:
“Go, post a lookout,
let him announce what he sees.
NRSVCE.7:
When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs,
riders on donkeys, riders on camels,
let him listen diligently,
very diligently.”
NRSVCE.8:
Then the watcher called out:
“Upon a watchtower I stand, O Lord,
continually by day,
and at my post I am stationed
throughout the night.
NRSVCE.9:
Look, there they come, riders,
horsemen in pairs!”
Then he responded,
“Fallen, fallen is Babylon;
and all the images of her gods
lie shattered on the ground.”
NRSVCE.10:
O my threshed and winnowed one,
what I have heard from the LORD of hosts,
the God of Israel, I announce to you.
NRSVCE.11:
The oracle concerning Dumah. One is calling to me from Seir,
“Sentinel, what of the night?
Sentinel, what of the night?”
NRSVCE.12:
The sentinel says:
“Morning comes, and also the night.
If you will inquire, inquire;
come back again.”
NRSVCE.13:
The oracle concerning the desert plain. In the scrub of the desert plain you will lodge,
O caravans of Dedanites.
NRSVCE.14:
Bring water to the thirsty,
meet the fugitive with bread,
O inhabitants of the land of Tema.
NRSVCE.15:
For they have fled from the swords,
from the drawn sword,
from the bent bow,
and from the stress of battle.
NRSVCE.16: For thus the Lord said to me: Within a year, according to the years of a hired worker, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end;
NRSVCE.17: and the remaining bows of Kedar’s warriors will be few; for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.

NET.1: Here is a message about the Desert by the Sea: Like strong winds blowing in the south, one invades from the desert, from a land that is feared.
NET.2: I have received a distressing message: “The deceiver deceives, the destroyer destroys. Attack, you Elamites! Lay siege, you Medes! I will put an end to all the groaning!”
NET.3: For this reason my stomach churns; cramps overwhelm me like the contractions of a woman in labor. I am disturbed by what I hear, horrified by what I see.
NET.4: My heart palpitates, I shake in fear; the twilight I desired has brought me terror.
NET.5: Arrange the table, lay out the carpet, eat and drink! Get up, you officers, smear oil on the shields!
NET.6: For this is what the sovereign master has told me: “Go, post a guard! He must report what he sees.
NET.7: When he sees chariots, teams of horses, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, he must be alert, very alert.”
NET.8: Then the guard cries out: “On the watchtower, O sovereign master, I stand all day long; at my post I am stationed every night.
NET.9: Look what’s coming! A charioteer, a team of horses.” When questioned, he replies, “Babylon has fallen, fallen! All the idols of her gods lie shattered on the ground!”
NET.10: O my downtrodden people, crushed like stalks on the threshing floor, what I have heard from the LORD who commands armies, the God of Israel, I have reported to you.
NET.11: Here is a message about Dumah: Someone calls to me from Seir, “Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?”
NET.12: The watchman replies, “Morning is coming, but then night. If you want to ask, ask; come back again.”
NET.13: Here is a message about Arabia: In the thicket of Arabia you spend the night, you Dedanite caravans.
NET.14: Bring out some water for the thirsty. You who live in the land of Tema, bring some food for the fugitives.
NET.15: For they flee from the swords — from the drawn sword and from the battle-ready bow and from the severity of the battle.
NET.16: For this is what the sovereign master has told me: “Within exactly one year all the splendor of Kedar will come to an end.
NET.17: Just a handful of archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be left.” Indeed, the LORD God of Israel has spoken.
